mainTopic: Squaring a city for the תחום שבת, and the geometry of the מגרש around the ערי לויים
overview: This amud deals with measuring areas around a city using squares and corners. First, a ברייתא teaches that when we measure the תחום שבת, we turn both the city and its 2000-אמה boundary into squares. At the corners, we add a full 2000×2000 square rather than measuring 2000 אמות on the diagonal. The ברייתא calculates that this gains 1200 אמות at each corner, and אביי says these numbers fit a round city 2000 אמות wide. The גמרא then brings a ברייתא about the ערי לויים: their area extends 2000 אמות, the first 1000 are a מגרש, and this מגרש is called 'a quarter' of the whole. רבא gives the פסוק as the source, and the גמרא asks how 1000 out of 2000 can be a quarter. Through a surveyor's calculation of areas, plus several objections, the גמרא shows that the quarter works out exactly for a round city: 9 out of 36. Finally, אביי begins a second calculation using a 1000×1000 city, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Square the city, then square the boundaries
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that we draw a square around the city, and then draw a square around the תחומין as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: One who squares a city makes it like a square tablet. Then he squares the boundaries too, and makes them like a square tablet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with the basic rule: to measure a תחום שבת, first box the city into a square, then box the 2000-אמה boundary zone into a square as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate squarings. First, the city itself is squared, even if it is round or irregular. Second, the 2000 אמות measured outward from it are also squared. Each squaring adds space at the corners, and the ברייתא will calculate those gains below.

keyTerms.meaning: שבת boundaries (the 2000 אמות around a city)

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One who squares the city
makes it like a square tablet.
And then he goes back and squares the boundaries,
and makes them like a square tablet.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both the city and its תחומין are measured as squares.

steps.title: How to measure at the corners
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא warns against measuring 2000 אמות diagonally from a corner. Instead, a full 2000×2000 square is placed at the corner.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he measures, he should not measure 2000 אמות from the middle of the corner, because he would lose the corners. Rather, he brings a square tablet of 2000 by 2000 אמות and places it at the corner along its diagonal.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and explains the correct method of measuring at the corners of the squared city.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you measured only 2000 אמות straight out on the diagonal from the corner, the result would be a rounded or cut-off shape, and the corners would be lost. Placing a full 2000×2000 square at the corner keeps the boundary a true square. Its diagonal reaches about 2800 אמות from the city's corner.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that 2000 אמות is measured in every direction from the corner. On the diagonal, the boundary actually reaches farther than 2000 אמות, because it is the corner of a full square.

phrases.english: And when he measures,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִמְדּוֹד מֵאֶמְצַע הַקֶּרֶן אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה
phrases.english: he should not measure two thousand cubits from the middle of the corner
because he would lose the corners.
Rather, he brings a square tablet

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהִיא אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה עַל אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה,
phrases.english: that is two thousand cubits by two thousand cubits,
and places it at the corner along its diagonal.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֶׁהוּא מוֹדֵד, לֹא יִמְדּוֹד מֵאֶמְצַע הַקֶּרֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the practical method for squaring the תחומין at the corners.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At each corner, a full 2000×2000 square is added rather than a 2000-אמה diagonal line.

steps.title: How much is gained at the corners
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא calculates the gains: the city gains 400 אמות at each corner, the תחומין gain 800, for a total of 1200.
steps.simpleTranslation: It turns out that the city gains 400 אמות on this side and 400 אמות on that side. The boundaries gain 800 אמות on this side and 800 on that side. Together, the city and the boundaries gain 1200 on this side and 1200 on that side.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by adding up how much extra distance the two squarings create at the corners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The diagonal of a square is about 1.4 times its side. For the city, squaring a 2000-wide round city makes the diagonal about 2800 instead of 2000, an extra 800, which is 400 per corner. For the תחומין, the 2000×2000 corner square has a diagonal of about 2800 instead of 2000, an extra 800 per corner. 400 plus 800 gives 1200 per corner.

keyTerms.meaning: It is found, it turns out
Here and there (in this corner and the opposite corner)

steps.whatToRemember: Squaring the city adds about 400 אמות per corner. Squaring the תחומין adds about 800 per corner. The total gain is 1200 per corner.

phrases.english: It turns out that the city gains
four hundred cubits here
and four hundred cubits there.
It turns out that the boundaries gain
eight hundred cubits here
and eight hundred there.
It turns out that the city and boundaries together gain
one thousand two hundred here
and one thousand two hundred there.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִמְצֵאתָ הָעִיר מִשְׂתַּכֶּרֶת אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת אַמּוֹת לְכָאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Calculates the result of the measuring method described in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The corner gains are 400 for the city, 800 for the תחומין, and 1200 in total.

steps.title: Which city these numbers fit
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the ברייתא's numbers are accurate for a round city that is 2000 by 2000 אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: You find this in a city that is two thousand by two thousand.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי clarifies what kind of city the ברייתא's numbers are describing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 400-אמה gain for the city only works if the city is round with a 2000-אמה width. Squaring that circle stretches its diagonal from 2000 to about 2800, which is 400 extra per corner. The 800 gain for the תחומין is the same for any city, but the city's 400, and so the 1200 total, depends on this size and shape.

keyTerms.meaning: And you find it (this case applies)

steps.whyThisMatters: Without אביי, the fixed number of 400 for the city would seem to apply to every city. He shows that the ברייתא is describing one specific example case.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
And you find this
in a city that is
two thousand by two thousand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the case in which the ברייתא's numbers are correct.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא's figures describe a round city with a 2000-אמה width.

steps.title: The boundary and מגרש of the ערי לויים
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי teaches that the תחום of the ערי לויים is 2000 אמות. The first 1000 are a מגרש, which makes up 'a quarter', and the rest is fields and vineyards.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי said: The boundary of the Levite cities is 2000 אמות. Take 1000 אמות of open space out of them. It turns out the open space is a quarter, and the rest is fields and vineyards.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about the ערי לויים. It also uses squares and corners, just like the ברייתא about city boundaries in the earlier steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The area around a Levite city has two zones. The first 1000 אמות must stay empty as a מגרש, and the next stretch is for fields and vineyards. The surprising claim is that the מגרש is only 'a quarter' of the whole area. That number is what the rest of the סוגיא will try to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: The 48 cities given to the לויים instead of a tribal portion of land
Open space around the city that must be left empty

steps.confusionAlert: Here the 2000 אמות is not the usual שבת limit. It is the size of the area given to the לויים around their city in the Torah's land laws. The math is similar to the earlier steps, but the topic is different.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Yosei said:
The boundary of the Levite cities is two thousand cubits.
Take out from them a thousand cubits of open space
— it turns out the open space is a quarter,
and the rest is fields and vineyards.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel case (ערי לויים) that uses the same kind of square-and-corner geometry as steps 1-4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Levite city boundary is 2000 אמות, and the first 1000 are a מגרש, which is called 'a quarter' of the area.

steps.title: What is the source for this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the 1000-אמה open space.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where the ברייתא's numbers come from. This sets up רבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the standard request for a source. The גמרא wants a פסוק that supports both the 1000 אמות and the idea that this comes out to 'a quarter'.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these words? (a request for a source)

phrases.english: From where are these matters?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ברייתא in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for the 1000-אמה מגרש and its being 'a quarter'.

steps.title: רבא brings the verse
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes the פסוק 'from the wall of the city outward, a thousand אמות all around'. The Torah is telling us to surround the city with 1000 אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The פסוק says, 'From the wall of the city and outward, a thousand אמות all around.' The Torah is saying: surround the city with a thousand. So the open space turns out to be a quarter.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question by quoting the פסוק in במדבר that sets the 1000 אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'סביב' (all around) tells us that the 1000 אמות must ring the whole city on every side. רבא then repeats the conclusion that this makes the מגרש 'a quarter'. That conclusion is what the גמרא challenges next.

phrases.english: Rava said: As the verse states:
"From the wall of the city and outward
a thousand cubits all around,"

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה תּוֹרָה: סַבֵּב אֶת הָעִיר בְּאֶלֶף,
phrases.english: the Torah said: Surround the city with a thousand,
so it turns out the open space is a quarter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source in step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'מקיר העיר וחוצה אלף אמה סביב' teaches that the city is surrounded by a 1000-אמה מגרש.

steps.title: A quarter? It looks like a half!
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that 1000 out of 2000 is a half, not a quarter.
steps.simpleTranslation: A quarter?! It is a half!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the number 'quarter'. On a simple straight line, 1000 out of 2000 is exactly half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you only measure outward in one direction, the מגרש takes up half the distance. So the ברייתא's word 'רביע' seems wrong, and it needs an explanation.

phrases.english: A quarter?! It is a half!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the 'quarter' figure stated in steps 5 and 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the מגרש is 'רביע'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Measured in a straight line, 1000 of 2000 אמות is half, not a quarter.

steps.title: The surveyor's calculation with corners
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains, in the name of בר אדא the surveyor, how to work it out for a 2000×2000 city. Counting in areas, the sides total 16 units and the corners total 16 units. The open space is 8 units from the sides plus 4 from the corners, which makes 12.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: בר אדא the surveyor explained it to me. You find this in a city that is 2000 by 2000. How much is the boundary? Sixteen. How much are the corners? Sixteen. Take away eight from the boundaries and four from the corners. How much is that? Twelve.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge by measuring area instead of a straight line, and by counting the corners too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side of the city gets a 2000×2000 block, which is 4 million square אמות, so the four sides make 16. The four corner blocks add another 16, for 32 in total. The open space is a 1000×2000 strip on each side, which is 8 in all, plus a 1000×1000 piece at each corner, which is 4 in all. That makes 12, which is far less than half.
steps.confusionAlert: The numbers 16, 8, 4 and 12 are areas measured in millions of square אמות. They are not distances.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: בַּר אַדָּא מָשׁוֹחָאָה אַסְבְּרַהּ לִי
phrases.english: Rava said: Bar Adda the surveyor explained it to me
— you find it in a city
that is two thousand by two thousand.
The boundary, how much is it? Sixteen.
The corners, how much are they? Sixteen.
Take away eight from the boundaries
phrases.notes: The 1000×2000 open strip on each of the four sides.

phrases.english: and four from the corners,
phrases.notes: A 1000×1000 open piece at each of the four corners.

phrases.english: How much is it? Twelve.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: בַּר אַדָּא מָשׁוֹחָאָה אַסְבְּרַהּ לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'half' objection of step 8 by switching to area and counting the corners.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מגרש is half, because 1000 of 2000 on a straight line is half.
steps.terutzMaskana: Measured as area with corners, the מגרש is 12 out of 32, which is much less than half.

steps.title: Still not a quarter: it is more than a third
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that 12 out of 32 is more than a third, so it is still not a quarter.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the open space comes out to a quarter? It is more than a third!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא's calculation. Even with the new math, the number does not match 'a quarter'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The total area is 32, and a quarter of that would be 8. The open space came out to 12, which is 37.5%. That is more than a third, so the ברייתא's 'רביע' is still not explained.

phrases.english: So the open space turns out to be a quarter?
It is more than a third!

steps.triggerLanguage: נִמְצָא מִגְרָשׁ רְבִיעַ? טְפֵי מִתִּלְתָּא נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the result of step 9's calculation.
steps.kashyaTarget: The surveyor's calculation as an explanation of 'רביע'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 12 out of a total of 32 is more than one third, not one quarter (which would be 8).

steps.title: Add the city's own area to the total
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the count by adding the 4 units of the city itself to the 32 units of surrounding area.
steps.simpleTranslation: Bring the four units of the city and add them on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem from step 10. It says we forgot to count the city itself, so we should add its 4 units to the total.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 2000×2000 city is 4 units (millions of square אמות). The earlier total of 32 counted only the area around the city. Adding the city gives a new total of 36.

phrases.english: Bring the four (units) of the city,
add them onto them.
phrases.notes: Add them to the 32 units already counted

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 10 by changing the total area.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Corrects the calculation by including a missing part (the city itself)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The total area is only the 32 units around the city.
steps.terutzMaskana: The total should include the city's 4 units, for 36 in all.

steps.title: Even with the city added, it is still a third
steps.stepSummary: 12 out of 36 is exactly a third, not a quarter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects to the fix. Even with the new total of 36, the open space of 12 is still a third, not a quarter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 12 ÷ 36 = 1/3. The goal was to show the open space is one quarter, which would be 9 out of 36. So adding the city did not solve the problem.

phrases.english: It is still a third!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The corrected total of 36 from step 11
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The open space is 12 out of 36, which is a third and not a quarter.

steps.title: The rule is about a round city
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the calculation is about a round city, not a square one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you think he was talking about a square? He was talking about a circle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection. It says the case is not a square city but a round one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now all the math treated the city and the open space as squares. If the city and the open space are round, the round parts take up less area. That changes the numbers, as the next step shows.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you think? (introduces a wrong assumption)

phrases.english: Do you think he was speaking of a square?
phrases.notes: He's pushing back on the idea that the city is square.

phrases.english: He was speaking of a circle.
phrases.notes: The city and its open space are round

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי סָבְרַתְּ בְּרִיבּוּעָא קָאָמַר? בְּעִיגּוּלָא קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 12 by redefining the shape of the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case (round instead of square)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The city and its open space are square.
steps.terutzMaskana: The city and its open space are round, so their areas are smaller.

steps.title: The math for a round city gives exactly a quarter
steps.stepSummary: A circle is a quarter smaller than its square. Take a quarter off the 12 units of open space and 9 are left, and 9 is a quarter of 36.
steps.simpleTranslation: How much bigger is a square than a circle? A quarter. Take a quarter off them and nine are left. And nine out of thirty-six is a quarter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא works out the numbers for the round city. Taking a quarter off the open space leaves 9, which is exactly a quarter of 36.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא uses the rule that a circle is a quarter less than the square drawn around it. So the round open space is 12 minus a quarter of 12 (3), which is 9. Since the total stays 36, 9 out of 36 is exactly one quarter, and the ברייתא's figure of רביע finally works.
steps.whatToRemember: The open space is exactly one quarter only if you picture a round city: 9 out of 36.
steps.confusionAlert: The rule 'a square is a quarter more than a circle' really means the circle is a quarter smaller (¾ of the square). That is why you take 3 off 12, not some other amount.

phrases.english: By how much is a square larger than a circle?
phrases.notes: Not a real question; it just sets up the math that comes next.

phrases.english: A quarter.
phrases.notes: The circle is ¾ of the square around it

phrases.english: Subtract a quarter from them —
phrases.notes: From the 12 units of open space

phrases.english: nine are left.
And nine out of thirty-six is a quarter.

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּמָּה מְרוּבָּע יָתֵר עַל הֶעָגוֹל? רְבִיעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Works out the numbers behind the round-city answer of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Calculation that confirms the redefined case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The open space is 12 units, a third of the total.
steps.terutzMaskana: Made round, the open space is 9 units, exactly a quarter of 36.

steps.title: אביי: The quarter also works for a 1000×1000 city
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the quarter ratio can also be found in a city of 1000×1000. He begins counting: the sides are 8 units and the corners are 16 units.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: You can also find it in a city that is a thousand by a thousand. How much are the side areas? Eight. How much are the corners? Sixteen.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers a second way to show the quarter ratio, using a smaller city. Here he only sets up the numbers; the rest of his calculation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side zone is 1000 long and 2000 out, so it is 2 units, and four sides make 8. Each corner is 2000×2000, which is 4 units, and four corners make 16. These are the building blocks for the calculation that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: The boundary zones along the sides

phrases.english: Abaye said: You can also find it
phrases.notes: He means you can also get that same one-quarter result.

phrases.english: in a city that is a thousand by a thousand.
phrases.notes: A smaller city than the 2000×2000 one

phrases.english: How much are the boundary zones? Eight.
How much are the corners? Sixteen.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ נָמֵי בְּמָתָא דְּהָוְיָא אַלְפָא בְּאַלְפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the round-city solution, אביי opens a new way to get the quarter ratio, using a smaller city (1000 by 1000).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The quarter ratio can also be shown with a 1000×1000 city: the side zones are 8 units and the corners are 16 units.
